item.title: GovBrief Today #550
item.description: Border agents swabbed a four-year-old's cheek and uploaded her DNA to the FBI's criminal database. Federal agents sent more than 2,700 records into that database every day last year, nearly a million in all, most from people never charged with any crime. Immigration enforcement now captures more profiles than any police force in the country, and the process could not be easier. All it takes is a cotton swab. No judge signs off, and agents swab nearly everyone they detain. Participation is required. A man who arrived for a probation appointment in Waco found ICE waiting, was ordered to open his mouth, prosecuted when he refused, and convicted. Genetic data sits in federal computers with no expiration date, and DNA never describes just one person. The four-year-old's file can be used to identify her parents, her siblings, and relatives she will never meet. I've emailed 8,501 stories over 550 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. item.title: I’m being strong for him. But I’m so fucking scared.
item.description:
CW: Cancer battle, description of treatment My partner of nearly 10 years starts fighting Stage 2 Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma in about 14 hours. It’s a mass on the base of his tongue the size of a strawberry, inoperable as it’s crossed the midline, and has spread to the lymph nodes on his left side. He faces 35 rounds of daily radiation to both sides of his neck and 7 rounds of weekly cisplatin chemotherapy. I’m the kind of person that fights anxiety with information. I hit the books. The subreddits. The studies. The survivor stories. I read statistics. 90% of people lose their taste buds, 25-35% never get them back. For the last 5 weeks, we’ve been doing a Taste Buds Food Tour, where we try new flavors and revisit favorites. Imagine if you knew in one month you may never taste anything again. What would you want to eat one last time? We’ve had Ethiopian, Greek, Thai, Peruvian, Vietnamese, Turkish, an all-you-can-eat seafood boil, a few brunch places, and revisited some old favorite places. I wish we had more time. He will have trouble swallowing. He won’t be able to eat solids after a few weeks, so I’ve been stocking up on pudding, yogurt, mashed potatoes, gravy, broths, and I’ve been making batches of homemade soup with extra unflavored protein powder mixed in, frozen in 1 cup cubes and vacuum sealed. (When vacuum sealed, frozen soup cubes are good for a couple years). I changed out his nightstand for a mini fridge so he has access to food and drinks constantly. Per his oncologists, he needs to eat 2500 calories a day to avoid getting a feeding tube. In one group I’m in, I polled 80 people about what their starting and end weights were for treatment, taking into account if they did radiation, chemo, or both, and if they needed a feeding tube. Of my very small 80 person pool of stats, the average weight lost for this treatment is 51 pounds. I even made him an NFC tag reader poster board for next to our bed in the event he loses his ability to speak due to tongue or jaw inflammation. He needs only to touch his phone to a specific tag to text me and ask for water, food, pain meds, burn cream, urgent help, that kinda thing. I work from home so I’ll be nearby, but I work for a medical call center so I’m usually chained to my desk with a headset and mic on and can’t always get up immediately. I couldn’t possibly be more prepared to be the best caregiver possible for him. And yet. And yet I still worry I missed something. I still know he’s going to suffer. I can’t take the pain away from him. I can’t prevent his neck from blistering. I can’t heal the cuts and sores that will form in his mouth. I’m so scared for him. The survival rate for this cancer is 85-90%. It’s just HOW he’ll be on the other side of survivorship that will be the thing. What will his quality of life be like? PSA: If you’re under the age of 45, GET THE HPV VACCINE. You never have to go through this, or cervical cancer, or penile cancer, or any of the other cancers that HPV causes with just a couple shots. If you have kids, get them vaccinated. 91% of all men and 87% of all women will get HPV at some point in their lives. There is no HPV test for men. Get the vaccine, friends.
Fuck you, cancer.
